rapport_notes: Friendly and professional, but somewhat mechanical in delivery; limited conversational warmth or personalization beyond logistics.
process_discipline_notes: Agenda question asked after probing had already started (location, square footage, floors all covered first), violating Stage 1 sequencing.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Let's start with a few questions. To get us on the right track. It should take about six to twelve minutes and then we'll be able to build you an accurate quote.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: And then do you have any specific questions or concerns in regards to this move besides pricing? [Asked after: location, apartment type, floor, walk distance, special items, fragile items, box count, destination location all already covered]
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'No, not really' to concerns. No follow-up on that response; rep immediately pivoted to logistics probing. No concern raised = N/A credit applies.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: We do have our no worries damage coverage. Which is our free evaluation coverage included in our hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: The second perk we have is our meet you mover feature and like many moving companies, or movers are not daily contracted workers. A few days before you move, you receive a meet your mover email introducing them to help ease detention of strangers arriving at your front door
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: and finally we do have our on time. Guarantee we value your time. So, if we can't make it in a time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.
evidence_quotes.communication: [Covered in Meet Your Mover segment: 'you receive a meet your mover email', but no day-before call, named crew lead, or inbox updates mentioned]
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: For Thursday September 17th, it would be an hourly rate of $190 for two movers and a 26 foot box truck. [...] we have a two and a half hour minimum. [Personalization: 'Both locations are a bit out of our range so that's giving you a trip fee of $210. [...] it would be $685 and then if we went into that three and a half hour range it would be $875.' — ranges given, but no framing of 'a typical 2BR takes X–Y hours, you'd fall toward Z' type anchor.]
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_estimate_is_window: Again I can send this all over. So, that way you have it like in front of you. [...] obviously there's a number of factors involved in terming mood time. So, like, if you can be prepared that obviously lessons the time and we can be more efficient.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_self_prep_tip: So, like, if you can be prepared that obviously lessons the time and we can be more efficient. So the last time we're there, the less money you pay as well.
evidence_quotes.close: [No rate-lock line: 'your rate locks when you book' never said.] [No explicit close ask: 'would you like our help with your move' or equivalent not asked. Call ended with 'do you have any other questions for me?' and customer said no, then rep said 'have a good rest of your day.']

top_strength: Rep delivered all four core differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, communication/prep tips) and framed them clearly without repetition across stages.
coaching_note: Ask the customer's agenda (concerns/questions) BEFORE diving into logistics probing—this was asked too late; also, close the call with an explicit booking ask ('would you like our help scheduling this move?') and mention the rate-lock benefit to create urgency.
